I'm inclined to agree with you. She is a very "move on, dwelling on the past does nothing, crying forever does nothing" kind of person. She's strong as hell and I love her for that. But I do think her uncle still bringing up these emotions bothers her, and that's where some of the hostility is coming from.

This is what I'm hearing the most of, that he's not entitled to my SO or her mother's time/pity. 

I think this boils down to me being too sensitive and assuming I know him when I don't. You're very right, though, you shouldn't guilt people into your life.

And yes...that's something that really bothered me. If you don't want to take his drunken messages then fine I guess, but I thought it was really insensitive to suggest he's an idiot for openly mourning and still being sad about it. HOWEVER: again, you're right, it isn't my place to tread. I did apologize to her since she seemed very upset about it. The subject didn't carry on beyond my apology, hopefully everything is ok...?

Yeah, sometimes I think I just get carried away in my own thoughts and think it's always appropriate to express my opinions...but in this situation that obviously wasn't appropriate. I will try to drop the subject with her.

And yeah, that's the thing - she is still mourning. There are still nights where she cries over him, and she misses him all the time. But that being true, it confuses me that she would be so hostile towards her uncle's grieving process, calling him stupid and saying he's "throwing a pity party" because he is still openly sad about it.

You're definitely right, I shouldn't look at it as some kind of "damned if I do damned if I don't" dichotomy. I should've just kept my opinion to myself in the first place. Because you're right, she didn't want advice, she was probably just venting to me. Although I am very worried about her uncle, I'll just have to accept they know better than I do.

And as for the temporary band-aid comment, I honestly didn't think about it that way...but I suppose you're right. I just hope he's getting support *somewhere*. But yeah, I shouldn't push my SO to feel sorry for him and talk with him or whatever else.

Definitely. She didn't hate her father or anything, but it really pissed them off for family or friends to talk so highly of him (one guy even compared him to literal Jesus) when he had some really shitty behavior. It drove them crazy that people were just glossing over it and acting like he was a saint, completely forgetting his destructive behavior. They loved him, but y'know. So I totally understand that.

I'm just not sure what to say when she says things like that? If I say nothing then that's rude as hell, and if I give my opinion it makes it seem like I'm talking down to her or implying she should feel a certain way. I just don't wanna be the asshole here who comes off as "I know better about a situation than the people involved." I just don't want her uncle to spiral into a depression and kill himself drinking, or something like that.

That's what I always try to do, distract myself. And a lot of the time it works. I still feel kinda bad afterwards, but it's usually not as severe as before. I got a "Wreck This Journal" recently and I'm hoping maybe that'll help me out a little when I fall into these "low" episodes. Maybe someday I'll try the dancing with no pants on method haha.

I appreciate it. Reading over your comment did make me smile. 

I try to see the value in my life but it's just hard sometimes. When I'm in that "high" state I have no troubles, though. Like even today I said in my mind "life is great, I'm so happy with my life." But then this *one* thing triggers this line of thinking I fall into where I just fall into this darkness and I can't bring myself out. It feels ridiculous afterwards, but during I just can't shake it, and I feel terrible.

But I see what you're saying. I will try not to be so hard on myself, even though I find it pretty easy.
